headline: US shares fell on Wednesday after a hotter-than-expected inflation report revived fears of more interest rate rises and deepened the sell-off in AI and chip stocks.
score_reason: Facts match the headline: a broad market fall on hot inflation and an AI-linked sell-off, confirmed by several outlets.
importance_line: Savers and pension holders with US shares lost money, and AI and chip investors lost most; the doubt is whether one day of falls marks a lasting turn.
summary: Yahoo Finance, The Motley Fool and Benzinga report that US shares fell on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026, with the Nasdaq Composite down 1.88% to 26,692.87 and the S&P 500 down 1.11% to 7,718.94. US consumer prices rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier, above expectations and up from 3.4% in August, which raised bets on another Federal Reserve rate rise and hit chip shares, with Nvidia closing down more than 3%.
notes: The Wall Street Journal original (wsj.com) returned HTTP 401. Entry built by the desk from Yahoo Finance (Nvidia chip sell-off article), The Motley Fool (midday report) and Benzinga via AOL; source set to AI News Desk because several outlets give the facts. Index closes are from the Benzinga/AOL text; the Dow figure was left out because the Fool page showed an intraday value.
